title: Studio Bookings
statement: A recording collective rents identical studios. Each booking in bookings is [start, end] in minutes, and it occupies a studio from start up to but not including end, so a booking ending at minute 10 frees its studio for another booking starting at minute 10. Return the smallest number of studios that lets every booking happen at its scheduled time.

examples.explanation: [0, 30] overlaps both shorter bookings, but [5, 10] and [15, 20] never overlap each other, so two studios suffice.
The second booking starts exactly when the first ends, so one studio is enough.

hints.content: The answer is the largest number of bookings that are in progress at the same moment.
That peak always happens at some booking's start time, so you only need to check start times.
Instead of re-scanning for every start, process events in time order and keep a running count of occupied studios.
Sort the start times and the end times separately. Walk the starts; before counting a start, release every booking whose end is at or before it.
Release ends with end <= start before taking the new studio, because the ranges are half-open. The maximum running count is the answer.

testCases.explanation: [0, 30] overlaps both shorter bookings, but [5, 10] and [15, 20] never overlap each other, so two studios suffice.
The second booking starts exactly when the first ends, so one studio is enough.
A single booking needs one studio.
[2, 10] overlaps [1, 3], [3, 4] and [9, 12] at different moments, and [9, 12] overlaps [11, 15], but no three bookings ever run at once.
Minute 18 is covered by four bookings.
Back-to-back bookings in any order reuse one studio.

solutions.title: Count overlaps at every start time
solutions.intuition: The number of busy studios only rises at a start time, so the busiest moment is one of the start times.
solutions.approach: For each booking's start t, count bookings with start <= t < end. Return the largest count.
solutions.pseudocode: best = 0; for each (t, _) in bookings: best = max(best, count of (s, e) with s <= t < e); return best
commonMistakes: Using t <= end, which counts a booking that has already ended at minute t.
Checking only end times, where the count has just dropped.
solutions.interviewExplanation: The demand curve only steps up at start times, so checking each start and counting the bookings covering it is correct. It costs n checks of n bookings each.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: For [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]], minute 0 is covered by one booking.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Minute 5 is covered by [0,30] and [5,10]; minute 15 by [0,30] and [15,20]. The maximum is 2.

solutions.title: Sweep sorted starts and ends
solutions.intuition: Only the order of events matters. If starts and ends are each sorted, a pointer over the ends tells how many bookings have finished before each new start.
solutions.approach: Sort start times and end times independently. For each start in order, advance the end pointer past every end <= start, decrementing the open count, then increment the open count for the new booking and track the maximum.
solutions.pseudocode:
starts = sorted starts; ends = sorted ends; open = best = j = 0
for s in starts:
  while j < n and ends[j] <= s: j++; open--
  open++; best = max(best, open)
return best
commonMistakes: Sorting with the default comparator, which orders numbers as strings.
Releasing only ends strictly before the start, which double-counts back-to-back bookings.
solutions.interviewExplanation: I treat the bookings as start and end events. Sorting each list lets me sweep time once: before taking a studio for a new start I release every booking that ended at or before it, because ranges are half-open. The running count of open bookings peaks at the answer. Sorting dominates at O(n log n). A min-heap of end times gives the same bound and also tells you which studio to reuse.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Start 0: nothing to release, open = 1. Start 5: ends[0] = 10 > 5, open = 2.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.content: Start 15: release end 10, open = 1, then open = 2. The best is 2.
